plainTranslation:
This person may help you find words for feelings you usually keep inside. Something about the way they listen, ask, or respond can make your inner world feel easier to name.

When this works, it can feel incredibly validating. You may start talking and realize they are following the emotional thread, not just the facts. They can help you understand why something affected you, why a small thing felt bigger than it looked, or why you could not simply "move on" when part of you was still holding the feeling.

There is a quiet intimacy in this. You may feel less alone with your moods because someone can meet them with language. They may help you hear yourself more clearly. Not by telling you who you are, but by giving shape to something you were already feeling.

The challenge is that words can move faster than the body. This person may name the feeling before you are ready to process it. They may explain what is happening inside you when what you really need is time to feel it for yourself.

Let the conversation help you, but do not let it rush you. The point is not to turn every feeling into a sentence right away. The point is to feel understood without losing touch with your own pace.
